scope: Independent whole-package offline review. No Julia, Julia query/parser/import/compilation/Pkg, numerical launch, launcher/seal/guard execution, old audit execution or synthetic script rerun. Fresh read-only Python hashing, text comparison and integer ledger calculations only.

findings.title: Signal every owned session member during cleanup
findings.detail: active_group_members includes both original PGID and the entire child SID, but signal_owned calls only killpg(child.pid). A descendant that moves to another PGID within the same SID is detected yet never receives TERM/KILL. stop_owned then waits indefinitely while that descendant can continue numerical work after the absolute deadline. --compiled-modules=existing does not prove this case impossible. Preserve the unreaped leader and identify/signal owned session members with start-tick/boot identity protection; use bounded cleanup with a preserved explicit failure if closure cannot be established. Do not report clean closure or start another numerical process while members remain.
findings.evidence: guard.py:155-184; launcher.py:27 waits without an independent timeout. Source-string session detection test covers enumeration only, not termination.

findings.title: Reject changed primary/master before sealing
findings.detail: seal.py copies whatever refs() returns into a newly accepted seal. refs() reads HEAD of the diagnostic and primary checkouts; neither seal nor launcher checks primary HEAD or refs/heads/master against host.json refs.master. A changed primary/master before sealing is therefore accepted even though master must remain 6f68e24e8ddac42b948da8fcc2d636c010751194. Require the frozen master and intended primary branch at sealing and launch boundaries, independently of the deliberately current diagnostic publication HEAD. Hashes of a few primary user files do not establish its Git state.
findings.evidence: seal.py:10-13; control.py refs; launcher.py:11,21,40. host.json contains the frozen master but no executable comparison uses it.

findings.title: Include entry validation in the total clock
findings.detail: The 750-second clock starts after initial seal hash checks, all 658MB of inventory checks, refs/host scans, reservation publication and output creation. This contradicts the stated inclusion of pin checks in wall caps and can admit a sequence whose entry-to-final duration exceeds the hard total while all current checks pass. Capture the total start at launcher entry before validation, propagate the same absolute deadline and refuse before spawning if validation consumes it. Report seal preparation separately if it is intentionally outside numerical-attempt timing.
findings.evidence: launcher.py:8-17 versus admission.md:22-28. Per-child checks and cost gaps otherwise count against their deadlines.

findings.title: Correct qualification row publications to 432
findings.detail: The 24 star cases publish 6*(6+6+30+30)=432 upper rows. The reported456 equals the selected term count 6*(7+7+31+31), not row publications. Correct the ledger without changing fixtures, arithmetic or any call budgets. The cost total91200selected product/subtraction pairs and96000reset assignments remain correct.

findings.title: Clarify the reservation boundary on preflight refusal
findings.detail: The admission says reservation is consumed on refusal or failure, but launcher seal/pin/output/host refusals occur before attempt-reserved.json is created. Such a refusal can be retried without consuming a reservation. Either explicitly define these read-only preflight refusals as outside the single numerical attempt or consume and preserve the attempt before the relevant admitted checks. Preserve no-retry behavior after reservation and never reuse partial output.
findings.evidence: launcher.py:9-16; guard/resource refusal after reservation does consume it.
